transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-16 10:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (NexaHealth MLOps), Carlos Rivera (Eng Mgr), Priya Singh (Security), Samir Patel (Data Scientist)

[00:00] Maya: Morning all, thanks for making time again. Quick agenda: verify access, confirm dataset, run short benchmark this week, and security follow-ups.
[00:18] Aisha: Morning. Carlos fixed the peering yesterday so we should be good to run tests, fingers crossed.
[00:28] Carlos: Yep I validated the firewall change last night. I'll drop the bastion host and CIDR in the CRM thread right after this call, 10.12.0.0/16 is current but I'll double check.
[00:40] Priya: From security side, we still need the KMS policy review and confirmation on audit log retention windows. I'll compile our SOC2 questions and share.
[00:52] Liam: For the benchmark, plan is 30 minutes on Dedicated with three concurrency levels 10/25/50, measure p50/p95, tokens/sec, and cost per 1k tokens. We'll run fp16 and q4.
[01:08] Samir: On quality we ran a smoke yesterday against hosted and saw about 6% bad responses on diagnosis extraction where trailing meds were dropped. We're worried about truncation behavior.
[01:24] Maya: Okay that's helpful context. Liam, suggestions to reduce truncation hits?
[01:30] Liam: Two paths: increase context window or chunk and stitch, plus tweak system prompts and truncation policy to preserve trailing meds. Also compare fp16 vs q4 because quantization sometimes affects generation behavior.
[01:50] Carlos: If we increase context to 2k tokens, what latency delta should we expect? Our triage UI needs sub-700ms median ideally.
[02:02] Liam: Depends on concurrency; rough internal numbers show median increased ~30% moving from 512 to 2k, but with prefix caching and batching the p95 can be controlled. We'll put concrete numbers in the benchmark report.
[02:18] Priya: Also, for compliance, does Redwood capture token-level metadata in logs or just request-level?
[02:25] Maya: Audit logs capture request metadata and you can configure retention; for Private you can bring your KMS and we can show an architecture diagram of key flow. We'll attach the security packet.
[02:40] Aisha: Samir, for dataset we plan to send 50 anonymized examples mixing short queries and long clinical notes today. Format?
[02:49] Samir: We'll follow Liam's template. Liam, can you drop the bench template link?
[02:55] Liam: I'll drop a template link in the CRM thread after this call. Placeholder: https://redwood.example.com/nexa/bench-template
[03:05] Maya: Recap of immediate nexts: Carlos drops access details, Nexa sends dataset, Redwood runs the 30-minute benchmark Friday, Priya will share SOC2/KMS notes and we schedule security deep-dive.
[03:20] Carlos: No blockers from infra as long as I can post bastion details tonight.
[03:26] Priya: I'll compile SOC2 questions and email by Monday. Also please include an architecture diagram where keys live.
[03:36] Liam: We'll include the diagram and migration playbook for Private vs Dedicated timelines. Private usually 4-8 weeks depending on infra, Dedicated can be online in days.
[03:50] Maya: Anything else?
[03:52] Aisha: Nope, looks good. Thanks all.
[03:56] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in CRM with links and the benchmark spreadsheet when ready. End call.

Notes: Transcript contains some disfluencies and occasional misattribution, artifacts referenced: "Nexa benchmark template", "Redwood security packet", and a shared spreadsheet to be uploaded to CRM/drive.
